User story: As an admin, I want my query split into words regardless of case and extra spaces so that 'GET  mguser' and 'get mguser' find the same cmdlets.
Expected behaviour: queryTokens lower-cases the query, splits on any run of whitespace and drops empty pieces (sources.ts:51). Names are compared against lower-cased copies (search.worker.ts:42,171). Leading, trailing and repeated spaces add no tokens. A whitespace-only query yields zero tokens and is no query at all: every row is listed in index order, the count label shows no '· N ms' timing because App.tsx tests the tokens of results.q, not the raw string (App.tsx:192-193), and writeUrl leaves q out of the URL (url.ts:52). The same tokeniser drives result-name highlighting (ResultList.tsx:184-200). locate (ResultList.tsx:171-181) finds each token literally, or else ignoring hyphens on both sides, and maps the hit back to the name's own characters. Overlapping marks are sorted by start, and at the same start the longer one wins (ResultList.tsx:189), so 'get get-mguser' highlights the whole 'Get-MgUser'. A token matched only by the typo fallback (SRCH-07) gets no <mark>.
How to test: 1) Open / and wait for the results. Type 'GET-MGUSER', then replace it with '  get-mguser  '. Both give the same count ('573 results') and the same order, and the first row is Get-MgUser with the whole name in a <mark>. 2) Search 'get get-mguser'. On the first row, Get-MgUser, the whole name 'Get-MgUser' is in a single <mark>, not just 'Get'. 3) Clear the box and type three spaces. The count reads '40,997 results' with no '· N ms', the URL stays '/' (no q parameter), and the list is the same as with an empty box (first row Add-MgApplicationKey).
Test result: Ran Playwright against :4400 at 1440x900 and 390x844, dark and light. 'GET-MGUSER' and '  get-mguser  ' both give 5,339 results with the same order; the first row is Get-MgUser with <mark>Get-MgUser</mark>. 'get   mguser' gives 2,287 with both tokens marked. Mark contrast is fine in both themes and nothing overflows at 390. Whitespace-only '   ' gives 40,931 rows like an empty query, but the label reads '40,931 results · 13 ms' and the URL becomes /?q=+++.
Errors found:
SRCH-01.E1 [logic/low] A whitespace-only query does not behave like an empty query. The tokens are empty, so the rows are right, but the count label still shows the '· N ms' timing because App.tsx tests results.q (the raw string) rather than the tokens. The URL is written as ?q=+++, so the blank query also survives reloads and shared links. REPRO: Open http://localhost:4400, wait for the results, then type three spaces into the search box. Observed: '40,931 results · 13 ms' and the URL is /?q=+++. Expected: '40,931 results' with no timing and no q parameter, the same as an empty box.
SRCH-01.E2 [ux/low] Highlighting drops overlapping tokens by start position only. When a short token and a longer token start at the same spot, the short one wins and the longer, more relevant match is not highlighted. REPRO: Search 'get get-mguser'. Observed: the first row Get-MgUser highlights only 'Get'. Expected: the whole 'Get-MgUser' (the exact match) highlighted.
Fix:
SRCH-01.E1: fixed in 487f99b (layer 2)
SRCH-01.E2: fixed in 487f99b (layer 2)

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet whose name I typed exactly to appear at the top so that I can open it immediately.
Expected behaviour: A token equal to the full lower-cased name scores 1000, the highest per-token score (search.worker.ts:89). Results are sorted by total score descending (search.worker.ts:189), so an exact match outranks any prefix match (at most 800) of the same token.
How to test: Open /?s=graph&q=get-mguser. The first row is Get-MgUser, ahead of Get-MgUserById, Get-MgUserChat and the other Get-MgUser* names.
Test result: Clicked the Graph scope and searched 'get-mguser'. The first rows are Get-MgUser, Get-MgUserById and Get-MgUserChat (5,337 results). A Node re-implementation of scoreToken over the dist index matches the UI order exactly: exact 1000, then prefixes at 796.

User story: As an admin, I want names that start with what I typed ranked highly, with the closest-length name first, so that partial typing quickly lands on the right cmdlet.
Expected behaviour: If the name starts with the token, score = 800 - min(100, nameLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:90). Shorter names that start with the token rank higher. The penalty caps at 100, so a prefix match scores at least 700: it is never below a noun-prefix match (at most 700, a tie broken by length) and always beats a substring match (at most 520). Ties are broken by shorter name length, then by ref, which is source order in SOURCES and then index order (search.worker.ts:186,189).
How to test: Search 'get-mgus' (573 results). The rows start with Get-MgUser (score 798), then Get-MgUserById and Get-MgUserChat, then Get-MgUserCount and Get-MgUserDelta, in non-decreasing name length. No row whose name only contains 'get-mgus' later in the name appears above a row whose name starts with it.
Test result: Searched 'get-mgus': 7,473 results. In the simulation, the first 573 rows are all prefix matches with name length never decreasing. No prefix row appears after row 573; the first non-prefix row is Get-MgBetaUser (fuzzy). The UI shows the same top 12 rows.

User story: As an admin, I want to type just the noun (e.g. 'mailbox') and see cmdlets whose noun starts with it so that I can find all verbs for an object without knowing the verb.
Expected behaviour: The noun is the lower-cased name after the first hyphen, but only when that hyphen is not at position 0. Names without a hyphen have an empty noun (search.worker.ts:51). If the noun starts with the token, score = 700 - min(100, nounLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:91-92). Name-prefix matches are checked first and take precedence (search.worker.ts:90).
How to test: Open /?s=exchange&q=mailbox (162 results). The first nine rows are the cmdlets whose noun is exactly 'Mailbox' (score 700): Get-, New- and Set-Mailbox first as the shortest, then Enable-, Remove-, Search-, Connect-, Disable- and Restore-Mailbox. After them come longer nouns such as Get-MailboxPlan and, further down, Get-MailboxPermission.
Test result: In the Exchange scope, searching 'mailbox' gives Get, New, Set, Enable, Remove, Search, Connect, Disable and Restore-Mailbox (all noun 700). Get-MailboxPlan and the other longer nouns follow. All scope behaves the same (718 results).

Feature: Substring match anywhere in the name
User story: As an admin, I want a word found inside a cmdlet name to match even if it is not at the start of the verb or noun so that I can find cmdlets by any part of their name.
Expected behaviour: If the token occurs anywhere in the lower-cased name, score = 520 - min(120, position) (search.worker.ts:93-94). Earlier occurrences rank higher, with a floor of 400. This is always below prefix and noun-prefix matches (at least 600).
How to test: 1) Open /?s=exchange&q=mailbox. Get-CASMailbox ('mailbox' at position 7, score 513) is listed after every row whose noun starts with 'mailbox' (the first 98 rows). 2) Search 'permission'. Rows such as Add-ADPermission and Get-MailboxPermission appear: the token is a substring of the noun, and no noun starts with 'permission'.
Test result: Searching 'permission' (874 results): the top rows are Add-ADPermission and Get-ADPermission (substring score 514). In the simulation, no row has a noun or name starting with 'permission', so there is no higher class to outrank. Get-MailboxPermission is a substring hit at index 27 (All) and index 6 (Exchange).

User story: As an admin, I want to type 'getmguser' without the hyphen so that I can search quickly without punctuation.
Expected behaviour: Each name also has a hyphen-stripped form (search.worker.ts:14,50). The token is stripped of hyphens too. The flat comparison runs only when the token contained a hyphen or the stripped token is at least 4 characters long (search.worker.ts:95-96). A hit scores 480 - min(120, position) (search.worker.ts:97-98), below a real substring match. Tokens of 1-3 characters without hyphens skip this step. A token with misplaced hyphens (e.g. 'get-mg-user') still matches through the flat form. Because the typo fallback only runs for tokens with no literal match (SRCH-07), the hyphenated and hyphenless forms return the same result set. The highlighter matches hyphenless tokens too and maps them back onto the name, so 'getmguser' marks 'Get-MgUser' (ResultList.tsx:171-181).
How to test: Search 'get-mguser' and note the count (573 results). Search 'getmguser'. The count is again 573, Get-MgUser is the first row, and its whole name is in a <mark>. Search 'get-mg-user'. Get-MgUser is still the first row, with the same count and the same highlight.
Test result: 'getmguser' and 'get-mg-user' each give 573 results with Get-MgUser first (flat match, score 480). Hyphenless results are not highlighted (no <mark>), which is consistent with the literal-only highlighter.
Errors found: SRCH-06.E1 [ux/low] Hyphenless and misplaced-hyphen queries return a very different result set from the hyphenated form, and the matched part is not highlighted. 'getmguser' gives 573 results, while 'get-mguser' gives 5,339, mostly fuzzy noise. A user has no visual cue for why a row matched. REPRO: Search 'get-mguser', then 'getmguser'. Observed: the counts are 5,339 and 573, and no row of the second search shows any <mark>.

User story: As an admin, I want slightly misspelled queries to still find cmdlets so that a typo mid-task does not return nothing.
Expected behaviour: Typo tolerance is an edit-distance fallback that applies only to a token that occurs literally nowhere in scope. Literally means as a name, prefix, noun-prefix, substring or flat match, or in a loaded description, counting only rows that pass the filters. Such a token is marked misspelt for the whole search and typo-scored for every row (search.worker.ts:174-175,182). The typo budget is 0 edits below 5 letters, 1 edit for 5-10 letters and 2 beyond (search.worker.ts:105). prefixDistance counts insertions, deletions, substitutions and swaps of adjacent letters (a swap counts as one edit). It measures the distance from the token to the closest prefix of the name, of the noun or of the hyphen-free name (search.worker.ts:112-132,139-143). Within budget, score = 300 - 100*edits - min(60, nameLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:144): about 140-200 for one edit and 40-100 for two (a name shorter than the token adds the difference back). Typo matches never mix with literal matches of the same token, so they cannot crowd out real hits. A typo-matched token is not highlighted.
How to test: 1) Search 'get-mgsuer' (swapped letters). Get-MgUser is the first row, followed by other Get-MgUser* names (681 results), and no row has a <mark>. 2) Search 'get-mgusr' (dropped letter). Get-MgUser is the first row. 3) Search 'get-mguser'. The 573 results are all literal matches, with no typo rows mixed in. 4) Search 'xyzq'. It is 4 letters, so there is no typo budget, and the result is '0 results' with the 'No match for “xyzq”.' empty state.
Test result: 'get-mgusr' finds Get-MgUser first (fuzzy 185); 'xyzq' gives 0. However, the simulation shows fuzzy accounts for 4,766 of the 5,339 results for 'get-mguser' and all 5,932 for 'get-mgusr'. A transposition such as 'get-mgsuer' gives 3,543 results led by Get-MgSecurityAlert and does not contain Get-MgUser. 'gte-mguser' and 'get-mg-usr' give 0.
Errors found:
SRCH-07.E1 [ux/medium] The fuzzy threshold (45% of n(n+1)/2) is very loose for long tokens. A 6-character contiguous run plus scattered letters is enough to match, so an exact or near-exact query pulls in thousands of irrelevant rows and the result count is misleading. Fuzzy junk also outranks genuine description matches. Meanwhile common typos (transposed letters) find nothing useful and show thousands of unrelated rows instead. REPRO: 1) Search 'get-mguser'. Observed: 5,339 results, about 4,766 of them fuzzy, e.g. Get-MgSiteTermStoreSetParentGroupSetTermRelationSet. 2) Search 'get-mgsuer'. Observed: 3,543 results led by Get-MgSecurityAlert, and Get-MgUser is absent. 3) Search 'retention' and scroll to the end. Observed: Get-MgBetaGroupThreadPostMentionCount (a fuzzy name match, description 'Get the number of the resource') ranks above Restore-AzSqlServer, whose description actually mentions retention. Expected: typo tolerance that finds the intended cmdlet without flooding the list. Possible fixes: a stricter threshold for long tokens, skipping fuzzy when literal hits exist, or an edit-distance approach.
SRCH-07.E2 [docs/low] The story says the fuzzy score falls 'between ~60 and 200'. The minimum possible is 120 + round(0.45*80) - 60 = 96. REPRO: Compute from search.worker.ts:117 with ratio 0.45 and a length penalty of 60.
Fix:
SRCH-07.E1: fixed in 487f99b (layer 2)
SRCH-07.E2: story text corrected (this file)

User story: As an admin, I want words from a cmdlet's description to match when the name does not so that I can search by what a cmdlet does.
Expected behaviour: If no name-based rule matched and descriptions are loaded for the source, a token contained in the lower-cased description scores 60 (search.worker.ts:100). This is the lowest literal score, so description-only hits sort below name matches. Before descriptions load (ldesc null, search.worker.ts:17-18,58-63), such rows do not match at all. A token whose only literal hits are in descriptions is then treated as a typo (SRCH-07) until descriptions arrive and the search re-runs.
How to test: After the page settles, search 'retention' (172 results). Name matches such as Get-RetentionEvent and Get-RetentionPolicy come first. The last 7 rows are description-only matches, starting with Restore-AzSqlServer, whose description mentions retention. Search 'retrieves'. All 209 rows are description-only matches.
Test result: Searching 'retention' gives 175 results after the page settles. The simulation puts the 7 description-only rows (score 60) last, starting at index 168, with no name match after them. The UI tail shows those rows with their description text. Delaying *desc.json with page.route gives 168 results before the descriptions load and 175 after, with row descriptions filled in.

User story: As an admin, I want every word I type to have to match so that 'user license' narrows results instead of widening them.
Expected behaviour: For each row every token is scored independently. If any token scores 0, the row is excluded (search.worker.ts:180-185). Matching rows are ranked by the sum of their token scores, then by shorter name, then by ref (search.worker.ts:186,189). Tokens may match different parts of a row (name, noun, flat name, description), so a row whose name contains one term and whose description contains the other is included. A misspelt token is typo-scored for every row (SRCH-07).
How to test: Search 'mguser license' (8 results). The first six rows have both terms in the name: Set-MgUserLicense first, then Get-MgUserLicenseDetail and the other *MgUserLicenseDetail* names. The last two, Remove-MgUser and Remove-MgUserByUserPrincipalName, have 'mguser' in the name and 'license' only in the description (700 + 60), so they rank below. Add a third token, 'mguser license zzzz'. The count reads '0 results', because 'zzzz' is 4 letters (no typo budget) and occurs nowhere.
Test result: 'mguser license' gives 20 results; adding 'zzzz' gives 0. Every row matches both tokens, but not always in the name. Remove-MgUser, Remove-MgUserByUserPrincipalName, Remove-MgBetaUser and others match 'license' only through their description. Get-MgReportTeamUserActivityCount matches 'mguser' only by fuzzy and 'license' only by description.
Errors found: SRCH-09.E1 [docs/low] The How-to-test step says every result contains both terms and none matches only one. In fact, rows whose names contain only 'mguser' (description-only 'license') appear, ranked above names that contain both literal 'license' and a fuzzy 'mguser'. This matches the expected-behaviour text but contradicts the test step. REPRO: Search 'mguser license'. Row 7 is Remove-MgUser (score 700 + 60), above Invoke-MgLicenseUser (156 + 511).

User story: As an admin, I want an empty search box to show all cmdlets in the current scope so that I can browse or just filter by facets.
Expected behaviour: With zero tokens, every row that passes the filters gets score 1 (search.worker.ts:180) and no sort is applied (search.worker.ts:189). Results are therefore in source order (SOURCES) and then shard index order. A blank or whitespace-only query counts as no query: the count label omits the '· N ms' timing (App.tsx:192-193) and the URL carries no q (url.ts:52). The no-match empty state wraps long unbroken queries inside the pane (.empty-title overflow-wrap: anywhere, global.css:398).
How to test: 1) Open / with the All tab selected and an empty box. The count reads '40,997 results', matching the placeholder 'Search 40,997 cmdlets'. No ' ms' timing is shown, and the first row is Add-MgApplicationKey (Graph). 2) Type 'get-mguser'. The label reads '573 results · N ms'. 3) At a 390x844 viewport, type 300 'a' characters. The empty-state title ('No match for “aaa…”.') wraps inside the results pane: .empty-title's scrollWidth is no larger than its clientWidth, and nothing is clipped.
Code refs: src/app/search.worker.ts:180,189; src/app/sources.ts:70-78; src/app/App.tsx:187-193; src/app/url.ts:52; src/app/chrome.tsx:189-199; src/styles/global.css:398
Test result: With an empty box in All scope, the count is '40,931 results' with no ms, matching the placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets'. The first row is Add-MgApplicationKey (graph index 0). At the Graph/Az boundary (row 27,327), the last Graph rows are followed by Add-AzADAppPermission. Scrolling to the bottom shows the last MECM rows, Update-CMClientStatus and Update-CMDistributionPoint, matching the index order. Typing a query adds '· N ms'. A whitespace-only query wrongly shows the timing (see SRCH-01). A 300-character unbroken no-match query makes the empty-state title overflow and clips the hint at 390px.
Errors found: SRCH-10.E1 [ux/low] The no-match empty state does not wrap long unbroken queries. The title grows to about 2,600px inside the results pane, so both the title and the hint line ('Get-MgUse…') are clipped at 390px. REPRO: At 390x844, type 300 'a' characters. Observed: .empty-title has scrollWidth 2619 and the text is cut off at the pane edge. Expected: overflow-wrap:anywhere, or truncating the echoed query.

Feature: Scope search to one source or all sources
User story: As an admin, I want to restrict searching to one product (Graph, Az, Exchange…) or search all so that results are relevant to the module I am using.
Expected behaviour: filters.source selects a Scope. 'all' covers every source, and a source id covers only that source (sources.ts:57-96). The worker searches only the loaded shards whose id is in the scope (search.worker.ts:172-173). The URL parameter is 's' (url.ts:15). Unknown or missing ids fall back to 'all' (sources.ts:94) and are then dropped from the URL. Per-source scopes have the placeholder 'Search N <Short> cmdlets' (sources.ts:85), and 'all' has 'Search N cmdlets' (sources.ts:73).
How to test: 1) Open /?s=graph&q=user, or pick the Graph tab and search 'user'. The placeholder reads 'Search 27,327 Graph cmdlets', the count is 6,016, and every row is a Graph row. 2) Open /?s=bogus&q=user. The All tab is selected, the placeholder reads 'Search 40,997 cmdlets', 6,731 results span all sources, and the URL is rewritten to /?q=user.
Test result: /?s=graph&q=user: 8,684 results, all rows tinted with the Graph colour (#9b8cff), placeholder 'Search 27,327 Graph cmdlets'. /?s=bogus&q=get: falls back to All, 16,834 results, placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets', 'All' tab pressed, bogus param dropped from the URL. Placeholders for az/entra/exchange/mecm are correct. The test step's '?source=graph' is ignored (10,301 results across all sources).
Errors found: SRCH-11.E1 [docs/low] The story's How-to-test uses '/?source=graph', but the app's URL parameter is 's' (url.ts:15). Following the documented link silently searches every source. REPRO: Open http://localhost:4400/?source=graph&q=user. Observed: placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets', 10,301 results from all sources, URL rewritten to /?q=user. Expected (per story): a Graph-only scope.

Feature: Facet filters (verb, module, category, extra, has examples)
User story: As an admin, I want to filter results by verb, module, category, API version/site role and whether examples exist so that I can narrow large result sets.
Expected behaviour: A row passes only if each non-empty filter equals the row's value exactly: verb, module, category and extra, and, when examples is true, the row must have examples (search.worker.ts:147-156). Filters are applied before scoring and when deciding whether a token is misspelt, and they combine with the query (AND) (search.worker.ts:175,179). The URL parameters are verb, module, cat, ver and ex=1 (url.ts:13-21). Module and extra are per-source facets: in the All scope they are dropped when the URL is read, so they never filter invisibly (url.ts:26-35). Switching source keeps only verb and the examples flag (App.tsx:139). An active filter value the scope lacks still has its select, shown as '<value> (none here)' so it can be cleared (chrome.tsx:161-165,181-182).
How to test: 1) Open /?s=graph&q=user&verb=Get (2,966 results). Every row starts with 'Get-'. 2) Tick 'Has examples' in Filters (or add &ex=1). The count drops to 505, and opened rows show examples. 3) Open /?s=graph&q=user&ver=beta (3,591 results). Every row carries the 'beta' tag. 4) Open /?s=az&verb=Approve (9 results) and click the Entra tab. The count reads 0 results with 'Nothing matches these filters.', and the Verb select shows 'Approve (none here)'. Picking 'Any' restores the results. 5) Open /?module=Az.Compute. The URL is rewritten to '/', the count shows all 40,997 results, and the Filters chip shows no count.
Test result: Graph 'user': 8,684 results. Verb=Get gives 4,083, all rows Get-*. Has examples gives 646. API=beta gives 360, all Get-MgBeta*. The opened row shows an Examples block. Filters combine with AND and are written to the URL (verb, ex, ver).
Errors found:
SRCH-12.E1 [ux/medium] A filter value that is not in the current facet list stays active but is invisible. The verb <select> renders blank (selectedIndex -1, neither 'Any' nor the value) and the list is empty. This happens when switching source, because setSource keeps the verb (App.tsx:111), and with stale or hand-edited links. REPRO: Open /?s=az&verb=Approve (9 results), then click the Entra tab. Observed: 0 results, 'Nothing matches these filters.', and a blank Verb select (the options are Any plus Entra verbs). The only way back is Reset or picking a verb. The same happens with /?verb=Bogus. Expected: drop or flag an unavailable verb, or show it as a selected '(not in this source)' option.
SRCH-12.E2 [ux/medium] In the All scope, module and API/extra filters from the URL still apply but have no control (the Module and extra selects are hidden for All). The Filters chip shows '1' and results narrow, but the user can't see what is filtering. REPRO: Open /?module=Az.Compute and click Filters. Observed: 292 results, chip 'Filters 1', panel shows only Verb=Any, Category=Any, Has examples and Reset. The same happens with /?ver=beta&q=user (5,258 rows, beta only). Expected: either ignore per-source filters in All, or show them.
Fix:
SRCH-12.E1: fixed in 487f99b (layer 2)
SRCH-12.E2: fixed in 487f99b (layer 2)

User story: As an admin, I want the filter dropdowns to list the values available in my current scope so that I only pick options that exist.
Expected behaviour: Each results message carries facets computed from all rows of the scoped sources, not narrowed by the query or other filters. Values are de-duplicated, empties are removed, and the lists are sorted with localeCompare (search.worker.ts:158-167,191). Verbs and categories are always provided. Modules and extras are provided only for a single-source scope and are empty arrays for 'all' (perSourceFacets, sources.ts:66-67,77,89). The filter bar shows Verb whenever there are verbs. It shows Module and Category only when they have more than one value, and the extra select only for a source with an extra label (Graph and Entra 'API', MECM 'Site role') and more than one value. Each of these is also shown while its filter is active (chrome.tsx:161-165).
How to test: 1) On the All tab, open Filters. Only Verb, Category, 'Has examples' and Reset are offered (no Module, no API). 2) Click the Graph tab. Module (Graph modules, alphabetical) and API (beta, v1.0) appear. 3) Click Az. Module appears, but there is no extra select. 4) On Graph, type 'user'. The Module and Verb option lists do not shrink.
Test result: All scope: the filter panel shows only Verb (99 values) and Category (sorted with localeCompare), and no Module or extra. Graph shows Verb, Module (83, localeCompare-sorted), Category, and API [beta, v1.0]. Typing 'zzzqqq' (0 results) leaves 83 modules and 54 verbs, so facets don't shrink with the query. Az and Exchange show no extra (none defined). MECM shows 'Site role' and no Module (only one module). This matches the UI's >1 rule.

Feature: Names-first loading, descriptions later with automatic re-rank
User story: As an admin, I want results as soon as the name index is loaded, with descriptions filling in afterwards, so that I can start searching without waiting for the larger description files.
Expected behaviour: The worker loads all name shards first (search.worker.ts:69) and answers searches once they are in. Only then does it fetch every source's description file (search.worker.ts:71-73). When they arrive, it re-runs the latest search under the same id (search.worker.ts:76), so the client still accepts it and description matches are added. Each results message carries described = every scoped source has descriptions (search.worker.ts:191). Before descriptions arrive, rows have desc '' (search.worker.ts:209) and show the module name instead (ResultList.tsx:162). While described is false, a query with no results shows 'No cmdlet name matches “<q>”. Searching descriptions…' (aria-busy) instead of the final empty state (chrome.tsx:189-191). A failed description fetch is swallowed, and that source keeps name-only search with no error (search.worker.ts:58-60). described then stays false, so an empty result keeps the 'Searching descriptions…' wording. While no results have arrived, the count reads 'Loading index…' (App.tsx:189-190).
How to test: 1) In devtools, throttle the network (e.g. Slow 3G) and open /?q=retrieves. The count first reads 'Loading index…'. Next it reads '0 results · N ms' with 'No cmdlet name matches “retrieves”. Searching descriptions…'. Once the *.desc.json files load, the list refreshes in place to 209 results with description text. 2) Block requests matching '*.desc.json' (devtools request blocking) and reload /?q=get-mguser. You get 573 results with Get-MgUser first, rows show module names in place of descriptions, and no error appears. /?q=retrieves then keeps showing the 'Searching descriptions…' empty state.
Test result: Held the *.desc.json requests with Playwright routing. The names-only search for 'retrieves' gave 0 results. After the desc files were released, the same search id was re-run (two results messages with the same id) and showed 209 results with descriptions in the rows. Aborting graph.desc.json gave name search 5,339 results for get-mguser, no alert, and Graph rows show the module in place of desc. A 500 on graph.desc gave 188 results for 'retrieves' (Graph desc skipped).
Errors found: SRCH-14.E1 [ux/medium] While descriptions are still loading, a description-only query shows the final-looking empty state "No match for 'retrieves'." and '0 results · N ms'. A moment later results appear. On a slow connection (graph.desc.json is 2 MB) the admin is told there's no match and may give up or rephrase. Nothing shows that descriptions are still loading. REPRO: Delay requests matching *.desc.json (devtools throttling or request blocking), then open /?q=retrieves. Observed: '0 results · 28 ms' and "No match for 'retrieves'." until the desc files load, then 209 results. Expected: a 'searching descriptions…' hint, or no definitive empty state until descriptions are in.

User story: As an admin, I want a clear message if the search index cannot load so that I know the site is broken rather than waiting forever.
Expected behaviour: fetchAsset aborts any artifact request after 20 s (sources.ts:23-24,34). Its error message is written for the reader, by cause (sources.ts:31-45). A network failure or timeout gives 'The server didn’t answer. Check your connection.' A 404, meaning a stale page whose build files are gone, gives 'This page is out of date: a newer version of PSIndex has been published. Reload the page.' User story: As an admin, I want a clear error if the details cannot be loaded so that I know to retry instead of seeing a blank pane.

Check your connection.'; HTTP 404 (a page from an older deploy whose build files are gone) 'This page is out of date: a newer version of PSIndex has been published. Reload the page.'; another non-2xx 'The server answered with an error (HTTP <status>).'; invalid JSON or a file without the row's record 'The server sent a damaged file.'. Try again reloads the file: a failed fetch is evicted from the module cache, so it makes a new request (a file that loaded but lacks the record stays cached and fails the same way).

Remove the abort and click the same first result again. The alert stays and 0 new requests are made. Only clicking result 2 and then result 1 loads the details.

For a deploy mismatch the fix is to reload the page, and the raw JSON parser message is shown to the admin. REPRO: Fulfil /a/*/data/** with 200 '{}' or '<html>' and open ?c=az:Get-AzVM. The heading is 'Syntax', with ' · N parameter sets' when there is more than one set. Each top-level group ('-Name <T>', '[-Opt <T>]', '[-Switch]') is a span.sg with white-space:nowrap, so lines break only between parameters; a bare <Type> joins the preceding group; brackets and angles are respected, including malformed '[-Status <StatusEnum]'. For New-CsTeamsVoiceApplicationsPolicy the h3 reads 'Syntax · 6 parameter sets', and the Copy on block 2 gives '[-AllowCallQueueWelcomeGreetingChange <Boolean>] ...' without the cmdlet name. User story: As an admin, I want a table of parameters with types and required/positional markers so that I know what I must supply.
Expected behaviour: Parameters parsed from all syntax sets are deduplicated by name and shown in table.params with columns Name (code.t-param '-Name' plus optional p.param-desc), Type (code.t-type with <wbr> breaks after '.' and before camel-case capitals; 'Switch' when no type), and a visually hidden 'Required' column. A parameter is Required (span.tag.tag-req) only if every set has it and every set requires it; a mandatory positional '[-Name] <T>' counts as required. An optional positional '[[-Name] <T>]' shows a 'Positional' tag; otherwise the cell is empty. Required parameters sort first, pipeline/proxy parameters last.
